candidate_name_provisional: Counterfactual Benefit-Certified Refinement (CBCR) — PROVISIONAL, NAME NOT AUTHORIZED AS IS (see recommended_method_name_status)
candidate_mechanism_summary: A frozen/shared global segmentor produces an initial mask; an optional expensive refinement exists; BEFORE running it, a lightweight GT-free predictor estimates the paired gain DeltaQ = Q(refined,GT) - Q(global,GT); the prediction gates EXECUTE vs SKIP; harmful refinements can be rejected so the global output is preserved; routing may include compute/device cost; applied within shared multi-domain medical segmentation.
overall_label_meaning: major components exist; the exact formulation/integration appears different and a narrower contribution remains defensible

closest_prior_works.why: same problem framing ('was the refinement worth it?') and a paired coarse-vs-refined comparison with revert-on-failure, but POST-HOC and untrained
formalises value-of-computation = expected benefit of a computation minus cost, decided before acting
optimal execute/skip pass-on criteria before an expensive stage, with an explicit cost term
CATE = paired outcome difference — the identical formal target, outside imaging
medical, per-sample compute decision BEFORE the model, efficiency objective
multi-domain medical segmentation with learned routing
optimises an information-gain signal for a regional action (RL, not segmentation)

algorithmic_novelty_detail: The mechanism 'predict the benefit of a future computation, then execute/skip' is fully precedented (metareasoning 1991; cascades 2001/2021; learned deferral 2020). The paired-gain learning target is standard causal-inference machinery (CATE, 2019). No algorithmic novelty can be claimed for either.
problem_formulation_novelty_detail: The exact question 'should I keep the refined mask or the coarse one?' is explicitly posed and answered in segmentation by JFS (ICIP 2025), and in the abstract by metareasoning. The formulation is not novel.
system_integration_novelty_detail: No verified work unifies: a frozen shared multi-domain medical segmentor + an optional refinement gated by a LEARNED GT-derived paired-gain prediction evaluated PRE-EXECUTION + preservation-fallback + explicit resource/device cost + tiny-structure motivation. This is the strongest residual claim, and it is an INTEGRATION novelty.
evaluation_novelty_detail: Phase 22 already established an evaluation-frame contribution (paired per-case DeltaQ with an oracle ceiling and routing regret under a frozen decision rule). Reporting benefit-awareness under an oracle ceiling + routing regret for segmentation refinement is not yet standard practice, but it is an evaluation-methodology contribution, not a new metric.
exactly_occupied_components: shared / universal multi-domain medical segmentation (UniverSeg, MedSAM, MedSAM2, MedUniSeg)
mixture-of-experts / learned routing in medical segmentation (M4oE)
regional / coarse-to-fine / high-resolution refinement (nnU-Net cascade, SegRefiner, scale-aware SR)
segmentation quality prediction without ground truth (Laves 2018, EvanySeg, SDC)
error / failure prediction and abstention (Learning-to-Abstain, conformal risk control)
conditional computation / early exit / dynamic resolution
execute-vs-skip gating before an expensive computation, with cost (cascades; ACT; SkipNet)
performance-preserving efficiency gains as an objective (adaptive-inference theory)
resource / mobile / edge segmentation (MobileSAM, edge-adaptive nets)
tiny-lesion / small-structure segmentation and zoom refinement
apparently_unoccupied_combination: a LEARNED, GT-FREE predictor of the PAIRED refinement gain DeltaQ = Q(refined,GT) - Q(global,GT) for segmentation, trained as a direct supervised regression (not an RL reward, not a statistical pass-on criterion)
that prediction used as a PRE-EXECUTION execute/skip gate on an OPTIONAL refinement (so compute is saved, unlike JFS's post-hoc verifier)
explicit preservation-fallback that retains the global output when the refinement is skipped or rejected
unified with a frozen SHARED MULTI-DOMAIN medical segmentor and an explicit resource/device cost term
motivated by tiny-structure difficulty (not claiming the tiny-object problem itself as novel)

major_novelty_risks.risk: A reviewer identifies JFS (Moon et al., ICIP 2025) as already answering 'was the refinement worth it?'
major_novelty_risks.mitigation: state explicitly that JFS decides POST-HOC and thus saves no compute; our claim is the PRE-EXECUTION, learned, GT-free gate

major_novelty_risks.risk: 'Value of computation' / metareasoning is a 1991 idea; the gate concept is not novel
major_novelty_risks.mitigation: cite Russell & Wefald and cascades up front; claim only the segmentation instantiation and the learned paired-gain target

major_novelty_risks.risk: The paired-gain target is standard CATE; claiming it as novel would be rejected
major_novelty_risks.mitigation: cite Kunzel et al.; state that we instantiate, not invent, the target

major_novelty_risks.risk: Med-DANet V2 already makes a pre-execution compute decision in medical segmentation
major_novelty_risks.mitigation: distinguish the decision variable (expected Dice gain of a refinement vs crop/quantization policy)

major_novelty_risks.risk: 'Certified' implies a guarantee we cannot provide
'Counterfactual' implies causal identification that the paired design does not require
major_novelty_risks.mitigation: use 'paired refinement gain'; caveat any causal analogy

major_novelty_risks.risk: Device/resource awareness may be read as engineering, not algorithmic, novelty
major_novelty_risks.mitigation: classify device-awareness as ENGINEERING VALUE unless it is integrated with the benefit gate as an explicit utility term

major_novelty_risks.risk: The tiny-object problem itself is not novel (tiny-lesion survey 2024)
major_novelty_risks.mitigation: claim only how optional computation is ALLOCATED, never the tiny-object problem

required_reframing: Drop 'certified' from the method name -> use 'benefit-aware' (or 'gain-gated').
Drop or heavily caveat 'counterfactual' -> use 'paired refinement gain'.
Do NOT claim the gate mechanism, the paired-gain target, multi-domain modelling, or resource awareness as individually novel.
Position the contribution as a SYSTEM/INTEGRATION novelty, explicitly downstream of metareasoning, cascades, CATE, and JFS.
State the PRE-EXECUTION property as the primary mechanical difference from JFS (compute saving), and the LEARNED GT-free DeltaQ regression as the primary target difference.
maximum_defensible_claim_level_scope: scoped strictly to the unoccupied combination (pre-execution, GT-free, learned paired-gain gate for an optional refinement within shared multi-domain medical segmentation with preservation-fallback); Level 3 is NOT defensible
recommended_method_name_status_detail: 'Counterfactual Benefit-Certified Refinement' (CBCR) is TOO_STRONG on two words: 'Counterfactual' (paired design, not causal) and 'Certified' (no guarantee demonstrated). Recommended provisional rename: 'Benefit-Aware Refinement Routing' (BARR) or 'Gain-Gated Refinement' (GGR). PROVISIONAL_ONLY — a final name is a Phase-24 decision.
phase24_allowed_condition: Phase 24 may proceed to a NARROWED architecture specification ONLY. The narrowed scope is defined in phase23_phase24_design_constraints.json. No implementation, training or TEST access is authorized by Phase 23.
